an4.46:1.4: When he said this, I, mendicants, said this to the godling Rohitassa:
an4.46:1.5: ‘Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’
an4.46:1.6: When he said this, the godling Rohitassa said to me:
an4.46:1.8: How well said this was by the Buddha—
an4.46:1.9: Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’
an4.46:2.1: Once upon a time, I was a seer named Rohitassa, son of Bhoja. I was a sky-walker with psychic powers.
an4.46:2.2: I was as fast as a light arrow easily shot across the shadow of a palm tree by a well-trained expert archer with a strong bow.
an4.46:2.3: My stride was such that it could span from the eastern ocean to the western ocean.
an4.46:2.4: Having such speed and stride, this wish came to me:
an4.46:2.5: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’
an4.46:2.6: I traveled for my whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—and I passed away along the way, never reaching the end of the world.
an4.46:3.1: It’s incredible, sir! It’s amazing, sir!
an4.46:3.2: How well said this was by the Buddha:
an4.46:3.3: ‘Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’
an4.46:3.4: When he said this, I, mendicants, said this to the godling Rohitassa:
an4.46:4.1: ‘Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’
an4.46:4.2: But I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.
an4.46:4.3: For it is in this fathom-long carcass with its perception and mind that I describe the world, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

an4.46:5.3: But without reaching the end of the world,
an4.46:6.1: So an intelligent person, understanding the world,
an4.46:6.2: has completed the spiritual journey and gone to the end of the world.
an4.46:6.3: Assuaged, knowing the end of the world,
an4.46:6.4: they do not hope for this world or the next.”
